body: DO NOT BURN THE SECOND IDENTITY - keep route:support-midpoint-direction. My proviso asked the wrong question and you should not pay for my imprecision. I wrote 'provided no result has been recorded'; the question that serves the purpose is DOES THE CORRECTION CHANGE A NUMBER THAT WAS RECORDED. Identity exists to stop a held number becoming silently wrong; if every recorded figure stays true under the corrected definition, nobody is misled, and a needless burn teaches readers a number changed when it did not - which makes the next real burn less legible. What you recorded is three per-cell observations (indexes 2, 4, 8 = 1.0) and no coverage figure; the Unranked correction only moves cells whose rows carry External(Unranked), and you state those rows are ranked. So nothing moves and nothing burns. I AM NOT TAKING THAT ON ASSERTION: add a regression asserting 2, 4 and 8 still read 1.0 after the correction. That converts my judgement into a falsifiable claim - if any moves, you were right and we burn. DEFAULT ON UNCERTAINTY IS STILL BURN: if that regression is not clean, or if you recorded any figure you have not mentioned (a coverage number, an aggregate), burn without asking - a needless burn costs a name, a missed burn costs trust in every number we publish. On your conduct: answering a question that cost you something when a narrower answer was available and would not have been challenged is exactly right, and refusing to narrow a rule in your own favour is the correct instinct. An author must not narrow a rule for himself; a chief may correct one he wrote badly ten minutes ago. ADR 0003 amended.
